RagShortTexts: Jerusalem encompasses the Holy Sepulchre and Temple Mount, venerated across three Abrahamic.

Variants.Content: Jerusalem lay at the centre of the medieval map, and its shrines drew pilgrims from every Christian kingdom. The Holy Sepulchre enclosed the rock of Calvary and the empty tomb, while the Dome of the Rock crowned the Temple Mount in Muslim hands. Khwarazmian horsemen sacked the city in 1244, and it never returned to lasting Christian rule. Its walls had decayed and many towers stood in ruins, yet pilgrims still made the journey. They paid tolls at the gates and braved desert heat and brigands on the road from the coast to walk the Via Dolorosa. The city's economy rested on that trade, on hospices and on the customs levied on every group of visitors, so each pilgrim band meant revenue for local officials and merchants who sold relics and candles.
Kneeling at Golgotha represents the ultimate cleansing of worldly sin. Weeping penitents hold olivewood crosses before the Tomb of Christ, lighting tapers in the crypt to beg for divine mercy.

No Christian banner flies over Jerusalem today, and officers at the gates collect the entry fees in silver groats. Sentries count every pilgrim who enters and leaves. Walk beyond the olive groves alone and Bedouin horsemen will take your mount, your purse and your linen. Carry a sword, and travel only in company with the caravan.
